title: Getting started with BayesianBenter
text: Benter model (1994) generalization Plackett-Luce model rankings. ranking built sequentially: stage rr next item drawn still available probability proportional λjαr\lambda_j^{\alpha_r}, λj>0\lambda_j > 0 item’s worth αr∈(0,1]\alpha_r \(0, 1] stage-specific dampening (noise) exponent. Setting αr=1\alpha_r = 1 recovers Plackett-Luce; smaller αr\alpha_r flattens choice probabilities, encoding idea rankers discriminate less sharply later stages. identifiability fix α1=1\alpha_1 = 1 report worths sum--one scale.

title: Getting started with BayesianBenter
Getting started with BayesianBenter
text: gibbsBenter() single entry point. Supply data pi, number items J, Gamma(, b) prior worths, Beta(c, d) prior dampening exponents. returned object stores posterior draws (fit$lambda, fit$alpha) plus sampler diagnostics fit$parameters.
code: fit <- gibbsBenter(pi, J = 5, a = 1, b = 1, c = 1, d = 1,                    iters = 2000, burnin = 0.5)  rbind(truth = lambda, posterior_mean = colMeans(fit$lambda)) #>                     [,1]      [,2]      [,3]      [,4]       [,5] #> truth          0.4000000 0.2400000 0.1600000 0.1200000 0.08000000 #> posterior_mean 0.4278881 0.1969852 0.1743369 0.1163316 0.08445811 rbind(truth = alpha,  posterior_mean = colMeans(fit$alpha)) #>                [,1]      [,2]      [,3]      [,4] #> truth             1 0.8000000 0.5000000 0.3000000 #> posterior_mean    1 0.8265617 0.5469033 0.3759476 op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1)) matplot(fit$lambda, type = "l", lty = 1, xlab = "iteration", ylab = expression(lambda)) matplot(fit$alpha[, -1], type = "l", lty = 1, xlab = "iteration", ylab = expression(alpha)) par(op)

title: Getting started with BayesianBenter
text: Partial (top-RR) rankings handled function: leave unranked positions NA (pass matrix fewer J columns). top 3 items observed, alpha_4 identified returned NA; item worths five items still estimated.
code: pi_partial <- pi pi_partial[, 4:5] <- NA        # keep only the top 3 of each ranking fit_p <- gibbsBenter(pi_partial, J = 5, a = 1, b = 1, c = 1, d = 1,                      iters = 1000, burnin = 0.5)  # only dampening parameters up to the deepest observed rank are estimated colMeans(fit_p$alpha) #> [1] 1.0000000 0.8310340 0.5501744        NA fit_p$parameters$R_obs #> [1] 3

title: Bayesian Estimation of the Benter Model for Rankings
text: BayesianBenter provides closed-form Gibbs samplers Bayesian inference Benter (1994) model ranking data. Benter model generalizes Plackett-Luce adding stage-specific dampening exponents αr∈(0,1]\alpha_r \(0, 1] -weight information later ranking stages: p(πi∣λ,α)=∏r=1J−1λwirαr∑j∈Rirλjαr. p(\pi_i \mid \lambda, \alpha) = \prod_{r=1}^{J-1}   \frac{\lambda_{w_{ir}}^{\alpha_r}}{\sum_{j \R_{ir}} \lambda_j^{\alpha_r}}. Estimation uses positive-stable frailty data augmentation restores conjugacy: item worths λ\lambda drawn exactly Gamma full conditionals, dampening exponent αr\alpha_r updated Metropolis-Hastings collapsed conditional. complete partial (top-RR) rankings supported single entry point.

title: Bayesian estimation of the Benter ranking model — gibbsBenter
text: Fits Benter (1994) model ranking data Gibbs sampling. Benter model generalizes Plackett-Luce model introducing stage-specific dampening exponents \(\alpha_r \(0, 1]\) -weight information later ranking stages: $$p(\pi_i \mid \lambda, \alpha) = \prod_{r=1}^{J-1}   \frac{\lambda_{w_{ir}}^{\alpha_r}}{\sum_{j \R_{ir}} \lambda_j^{\alpha_r}},$$ \(\lambda_j > 0\) item worths, \(w_{ir}\) item placed \(r\)th voter \(\), \(R_{ir}\) set items still risk stage \(r\). Inference uses positive-stable frailty data augmentation restores conjugacy, worths drawn exactly Gamma full conditionals \(\alpha_r\) updated Metropolis-Hastings collapsed conditional.

title: Bayesian estimation of the Benter ranking model — gibbsBenter
text: pi ranking data set: integer matrix (data frame, single vector interpreted one ranking) one ranking per row. Entry pi[, r] item placed rth voter ; ranked entries left-aligned unranked tail positions NA. non-missing entries must integers 1:J repeats within row. J Integer (>= 3). total number items ranked. , b Shape rate Gamma(, b) prior item worths \(\lambda_j\). identified (sum--one) scale, alone controls induced symmetric Dirichlet prior normalized worths; b sets (marginalized-) overall scale. c, d Shape parameters Beta(c, d) prior dampening exponent \(\alpha_r\), r=2,...,J-1. (alpha_1 fixed 1 identifiability.) alpha_min Lower floor Metropolis-Hastings proposals \(\alpha_r\). Proposals alpha_min rejected. small positive value (e.g. 0.05) keeps alpha_r inside range tilted-stable sampler numerically stable; default 0 imposes floor beyond open boundary. iters Number Gibbs iterations (including burn-). mh_iters Number Metropolis-Hastings sub-steps per \(\alpha_r\) per sweep. burnin Fraction iters discarded burn-. adaptive tuning proposal scales active burn-frozen afterwards. verbose Logical. TRUE, show text progress bar.

title: Bayesian estimation of the Benter ranking model — gibbsBenter
text: list components: lambda (iters - burn) x J matrix posterior draws item worths, normalized sum one row. alpha (iters - burn) x (J-1) matrix posterior draws dampening exponents. Column 1 fixed 1; partial data, columns beyond deepest observed rank NA. parameters list recording prior sampler settings Metropolis-Hastings acceptance rates. time_secs Wall-clock run time seconds.

title: Bayesian estimation of the Benter ranking model — gibbsBenter
text: gibbsBenter() user-facing entry point. validates standardizes pi, dispatches appropriate internal sampler complete partial rankings. length-(J-1) ranking pins final item completed automatically (deduction, imputation); row treated genuinely partial leaves two items unplaced. partial rankings, dampening parameters deepest observed rank identifiable, alpha_r stages beyond longest observed ranking neither updated returned (reported NA). item worths \(\lambda\) J items always estimated.
